body_truncated:
**rust-analyzer version**: `rust-analyzer version: 5d5bbec9b 2022-05-09 stable`
**rustc version**: `rustc 1.62.0-nightly (f1f721e64 2022-05-13)`

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26110087/168413920-268a1492-beef-44aa-8a53-2e19df5029d5.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26110087/168413924-14586651-3ff2-491a-8983-cbe3fed8a75c.png)

The cause of this issue is [`rewrite_url_link`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-analyzer/blob/master/crates/ide/src/doc_links.rs#L56) calls `crate_of_def` which [returns `None` if `def` is `BuiltinType`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-analyzer/blob/master/crates/ide/src/doc_links.rs#L352-L356) and [makes `crate_of_def` early return](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-analyzer/blob/master/crates/ide/src/doc_links.rs#L338)). 

I think one possible solution is to pass `famous_defs` from https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-analyzer/blob/master/crates/ide/src/hover.rs#L172-L175 down to `crate_of_def` to resolve BuiltinType to std crate via `famous_defs.std()?`.

Another solution is, since we already found the doc via [`find_std_module`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-analyzer/blob/master/crates/ide/src/hover/render.rs#L453), It should be possible to not only return the markup but also the doc owner from `render::definition` than pass it to `render::process_markup` https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-analyzer/blob/master/crates/ide/src/hover.rs#L176-L178 . This approch feels more natural to me but requires much more refactoring existing code.

VSCode: limit std suggestions outside tests when `#![no_std]` is conditional on `#[cfg(test)]`
body_truncated:
When writing `#![no_std]` libraries, it is often useful to disable this for test code (the library itself is fully no_std, but allowing e.g. `Vec` to be easily used makes testing easier and clearer). This is done using a "conditional no_std" attribute (e.g. `#![cfg_attr(not(test), no_std)]`)

Rust Analyzer currently doesn't handle this particularly well as it globally enables std imports and suggestions, not just inside test code

Example with conditional `#![no_std]`. Imports are from std even though this location is `no_std`
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8765278/164113692-8f9e22c8-5822-41cb-a057-f8689d909f81.png)

* I was expecting this to remove all std suggestions? `Str` isn't exactly text I'm normally getting suggestions for when writing for `no_std` so this was a bit of a surprise too

body_truncated:
**rust-analyzer version**: 2022-03-28

**rustc version**: rustc 1.61.0-nightly (c5cf08d37 2022-03-30)

Example:
```rs
fn main() {
  let x = '\\'.ok|
}
```
(where `|` is the cursor)
Accepting the suggestion will result in this code:
```rs
fn main() {
  let x = Ok('\')|
}
```
which is invalid syntax.

It also seems that this happens with strings. Other escapes are intact, it's only `\\` that gets mangled.

Also of note is that the escape may be nested in some deeper expression. For instance:
```rs
match x {
  true => '\\',
  false => 'a',
}.ok|
```

body_truncated:
**rust-analyzer version**: bc08b8eff 2022-03-28 stable

**rustc version**: rustc 1.59.0 (9d1b2106e 2022-02-23)

**relevant settings**: none really

This is a thorny one, hold on.

I tend to use eyre's [`eyre!`](https://docs.rs/eyre/latest/eyre/macro.eyre.html) macro a bunch. But I use it from projects that only have [color-eyre](https://lib.rs/crates/color-eyre) as a dependency.

`color-eyre` re-exports the whole `eyre` crate, as `color_eyre::eyre`. This results in suboptimal autocompletion in rust-analyzer. Say I have some code:

```rust
use color_eyre::Report;

fn do_stuff() -> Result<(), Report> {
  Err(eyre!("we could NOT do stuff! the all is lost moment!"))
}
```

This is an error since `eyre!` is not scope. Firstly, quick nit, pressing `ctrl-space` (to open up the autocompletion menu) doesn't do the expected thing if the cursor if _after_ the bang in `eyre!`. That's a papercut, but I've been using rust-analyzer for a while so I know to place my cursor after `eyre` but before the bang, _then_ trigger autocompletion.

And then I see this:

title: Hygiene not taken into account for name resolution (wrong type inference with `izip!`)
body_truncated:
In this line:
https://github.com/rust-analyzer/rust-analyzer/blob/69e5bd5a2532cfe47e5517d720eb70cbf3f4a908/crates/ide_assists/src/handlers/inline_call.rs#L347
we infer the wrong type for `expr`, namely we infer `Vec<PathExpr>`. The reason for this seems to be our expansion of the `izip!(params, param_use_nodes, arguments)` macro call:
```rust
$crate::__std_iter::IntoIterator::into_iter(params).zip(param_use_nodes).zip(arguments).map(|((a,b),b)|(a,b,b))
```
note the `.map(|((a,b),b)| (a,b,b))`. This seems to be a hygiene issue, where the different `b`s come from different macro expansions and so we need to consider hygiene to correctly resolve them.

Part of #8961.

In

title: Semicolon insertion breaks on complex function declaration
Renaming a module renames its file but not its directory
body_truncated:
1. Construct a project with files

    ```
    src/lib.rs         mod things;
    
    src/things.rs      mod foo;
                       mod bar;
    
    src/things/foo.rs  // empty
    src/things/bar.rs  // empty
    ```

2. Perform a rename on `mod things;` OR on the file `src/things.rs`.

In either case, the `mod things;` item and `things.rs` file will be renamed in sync, but `src/things/` will be left behind, causing `mod foo; mod bar;` to not find their files.

If the `things` module is instead defined using `src/things/mod.rs` then it is (correctly) moved into a new directory, but the child module files are left behind in the old directory.

"Fill struct fields" assist shouldn't be applicable if the struct has inaccesible fields
body_truncated:
As @matklad mentioned in [ERA08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n5LDjWIAByM&t=3825s), rust-analyzer should not suggest to fill struct fields if they are inaccessible.

Example:
```rust
use std::rc::Rc;

struct Struct {
    field: String
}

type Data = Rc<Struct>;

fn main() {
    let data = Data {};
}
```

It fails to compile with the following error:
```
error: cannot construct `Rc<Struct>` with struct literal syntax due to inaccessible fields
  --> src/main.rs:10:16
   |
10 |     let data = Data {};
   |      
```

Currently rust-analyzer offers to fill the fields, which results in following code:
```rust
let data = Data { ptr: todo!(), phantom: todo!() };
```

Of course it fails to compile:
```
error[E0451]: field `ptr` of struct `Rc` is private
  --> src/main.rs:10:23
   |
10 |     let data = Data { ptr: todo!(), phantom: todo!() };
   |                       ^^^^^^^^^^^^ private field

error[E0451]: field `phantom` of struct `Rc` is private
  --> src/main.rs:10:37
   |
10 |     let data = Data { ptr: todo!(), phantom: todo!() };
   |       
```

I'd like to fix this issue :)

title: `goto_definition` should not navigate to the local variable defined in macros.
“Expand glob import” generates invalid syntax if the glob is unused
body_truncated:
If a glob import is completely unused, then performing “Expand glob import” will transform valid code such as

```rust
use std::io::*;
```

into

```rust
use std::io::;
```

More correct behavior would be to do one of these:

* Remove the import (closer to canonical warning-free form of source code)
* Generate `use std::io::{};` (more regular, gives a cue as to what is going on rather than “silent” deletion, and will be deleted anyway by rustfmt if format on save is enabled)

---

Context: In the particular case where this came up, I was editing code exclusively targeting `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and for some reason those files weren't reporting “unused import” warnings at all (this is the first time I tried changing `rust-analyzer.cargo.target` to a cross-compilation target), so the _only_ assist available was to expand the import, not to remove it entirely which would have been a better option.

title: LSIF metadata has no tool info
body_truncated:
Currently, the `MetaData` vertex in LSIF dumps looks like this:
```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "type": "vertex",
  "label": "metaData",
  "version": "0.5.0",
  "projectRoot": "file:///fake/project/path",
  "positionEncoding": "utf-16"
}
```

The LSIF specifies a `toolInfo` property in the MetaData vertex which allows specifying the tool name, its version and what arguments were passed.
https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsif/0.6.0/specification/#metaData

This is important because Sourcegraph expects this field to be set when uploading LSIF data. When I set up uploads of LSIF dumps to sourcegraph in the CI of my project, I had to add a `-indexer=rust-analyzer` flag to the Sourcegraph CLI because it could not infer it from the MetaData vertex: https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-authentication-service/blob/29bf149921a6ce46775cb55fcfbf022f8ab25856/.github/workflows/check.yaml#L105

I opened a PR: #10519 ; with it, the vertex looks like this:
```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "type": "vertex",
  "label": "metaData",
  "version": "0.5.0",
  "projectRoot": "file:///fake/project/path",
  "positionEncoding": "utf-16",
  "toolInfo": {
    "name": "rust-analyzer",
    "version": "ed4b312fa 2021-10-11 dev"
  }
}
```

body_truncated:
<!--

Before submitting, please make sure that you're not running into one of these known issues:

 2. attribute proc macros are supported but not enabled by default: #6029

Otherwise please try to provide information which will help us to fix the issue faster. Minimal reproducible examples with few dependencies are especially lovely <3.
-->
Input:
```Rust
struct State {
    field: u32,
}

struct Db {
    field: u32,
}

fn testfn(state: &mut State, db: &mut Db) {
    // <wanna extract>
    state.field = 4;
    nested_fn(state, db);
    // </wanna extract>
    // Simulating access after the extracted portion
    state.field = 16;
    println!("{}", db.field);
}

fn nested_fn(state: &mut State, db: &Db) {
    state.field = 8;
    println!("{}", db.field);
}

fn main() {
    testfn(&mut State { field: 0 }, &mut Db { field: 0 });
}
```

Extract function generates this beauty:
```Rust
fn fun_name(state: &&mut State, db: &&mut Db) {
    state.field = 4;
    nested_fn(*state, *db);
}
```

When it should generate simply this:
```Rust
fn fun_name(state: &mut State, db: &mut Db) {
    state.field = 4;
    nested_fn(state, db);
}
```
Version: rust-analyzer version: 516eb40ba 2021-09-13 stable

title: Formatting with rustfmt no longer works in rustc repository
Plaintext textDocument/hover malformed
Expand Derive Macros does not update if the underlying proc macro changes.
body_truncated:
From the new feature #10014 (thank you so much for this btw, so helpful!) 

In a workspace where you might be working on a crate that implements some `#[derive(Whatever)]` macros, editing the proc macro functions do not seem to cause the expanded output to change (even after re-requesting a new expansion.) In order to view the new output of the generated code, you have to restart rust-analyzer. 

It would be *really* cool if rust-analyzer could detect that the proc macro crate has changed, and recompute the expanded macro output live. But at the very least, even if it was not live, re-running "expand macro recursively" should show the latest output from the proc macro.

title: False positive for snake_case lint when using bitflags macro
body_truncated:
<!--
Troubleshooting guide: https://rust-analyzer.github.io/manual.html#troubleshooting
Forum for questions: https://users.rust-lang.org/c/ide/14

Before submitting, please make sure that you're not running into one of these known issues:

 1. on-the-fly diagnostics are mostly unimplemented (`cargo check` diagnostics will be shown when saving a file)
 2. some settings are required for procedural macro and build script support (`rust-analyzer.cargo.loadOutDirsFromCheck`, `rust-analyzer.procMacro.enable`): #6448
 3. some platform-specific imports are not resolved: #6038

Otherwise please try to provide information which will help us to fix the issue faster. Minimal reproducible examples with few dependencies are especially lovely <3.
-->
```Rust
#[macro_use]
extern crate bitflags;

bitflags! {
    struct Flags: u32 {
        const A = 0;
    }
}
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1521976/112749331-fd88e780-8fc1-11eb-996c-a37de3341eb4.png)

This seems to be the relevant expanded code
```Rust
#[allow(non_snake_case)]
        trait __BitFlags {
            #[inline]
            fn A(&self) -> bool {
                false
            }
        }
        impl __BitFlags for Flags {
            #[allow(deprecated)]
            #[inline]
            fn A(&self) -> bool {
                if Self::A.bits == 0 && self.bits != 0 {
                    false
                } else {
                    self.bits & Self::A.bits == Self::A.bits
                }
            }
        }
```
Rust-analyzer seems to ignore the `#[allow(non_snake_case)]` attribute. Rustc and clippy don't warn about this.

RA version is 2021-03-22

title: Listing symbols does not see aliases
body_truncated:
Issue from [coc-rust-analyzer](https://github.com/fannheyward/coc-rust-analyzer/issues/636)

The problem is best illustrated as such:

We have a `struct Vec3;` and a `use Vec3 as Color` statement.
When running `CocList -I symbols` and searching for `Vec3` it finds it just fine but does not resolve `Color`.

This is apparently a limitation of aliases and has been discussed in libs zullip recently. Relevant [issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/21903) in the language?

title: "Extract into variable" action not shown when selecting macro invocation
Type checker does not eagerly select predicates from where-clauses
Error on DMatrix::zeros(rows, cols)
body_truncated:
For me (on current weekly version), this version introduced a regression that causes [`DMatrix`](https://docs.rs/nalgebra/0.21.1/nalgebra/base/type.DMatrix.html) to be picked up incorrectly when using [`DMatrix::zeros()`](https://docs.rs/nalgebra/0.21.1/nalgebra/base/type.MatrixMN.html#method.zeros-3). It claims that there is no arguments:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12789579/87883524-f858af00-c9d5-11ea-9722-aa1ec150f1f4.png)

However, a `cargo check` passes just fine, and I am actually building and running this code currently as part of another program, so it is certain that it does work. In fact, the last version did not have this issue.

My suspicion is that it is incorrectly picking up the first [`Matrix::zeros()`](https://docs.rs/nalgebra/0.21.1/nalgebra/base/type.MatrixMN.html#method.zeros). Nalgebra has four definitions of `zeros()` on `Matrix`, each of which may be used depending on which dimensions are `Dynamic` or which impl `DimName`.

I will let everyone know if this issue goes away on Monday.

title: Doc comment block should strip leading asterisk (*)
body_truncated:
In looking at `struct ClientCapabilities` of lsp-types defined as

```rust
/**
 * Where ClientCapabilities are currently empty:
 */
pub struct ClientCapabilities {
    // ...
}
```

I noticed that hover shows the comment as

> * Where ClientCapabilities are currently empty: 

In looking at https://docs.rs/lsp-types/0.61.0/lsp_types/struct.ClientCapabilities.html we can see  that it's rendered without the leading asterisk (or bullet in markdown).

My initial thought was that maybe we need to strip leading `*` off of block dock comments if present in `DocCommentsOwner::doc_comment_text` but that could also end up stripping markdown. Maybe it should be done in `format_docs` instead when we look for markdown... but by then we've lost all knowledge of the comment except for it's string contents.
